title: Execute KMS outage/degradation game day (staging + canary) and capture learnings
creator: Talia Benson
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS hardening + rotation
description:
Goal
Run a structured game day to validate Redwood’s behavior under KMS dependency failures (timeouts/throttling/IAM denies/disabled keys/region outage) in (1) staging and (2) one canary environment. Capture results, gaps, and follow-up work. This is the execution issue (planning doc + harness implementation are in ENG-4234).

Owners / participants
- Driver: Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- Co-driver: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Security: Marcus Lin (Security Eng), Kevin Osei (Security Eng)
- Platform: Ethan Park (Control Plane), Diego Santos (Cross-deployment)
- Observability: Allison Grant
- Release/Comms: Connor O'Brien

Pre-req checklist (must be green before start)
- [x] Failure injection hooks available in staging and canary (GitHub: redwood PR #28873)
- [x] Circuit breaker + standardized backoff shipped behind flags (GitHub: redwood PR #28741)
- [x] KMS metrics/tracing dashboards available (ENG-4239 scope)
- [x] Runbook drafted for dependency degradation (Confluence: /eng-sre/runbooks/kms-dependency-degradation-runbook)
- [x] Audit events emission enabled in test envs (GitHub: redwood PR #28805)

Target environments
1) Staging: shared staging control plane + data plane
2) Canary: canary-private-usw2-01 (Private) + one hosted canary tenant (hosted-canary-07) for parity checks

Comms plan
- 30 min pre-brief in #eng-sre and #eng-security with scenario list + rollback conditions
- During game day: live notes in this ticket + dedicated Slack huddle
- Post: summary in #eng-sre, #eng-platform, #eng-security with action items and owners

Scenarios to run (order matters)
S0: Baseline (no injection)
- Validate dashboards, alerting, and KMS health summary endpoint behavior
- Confirm cache hit rate + breaker state are stable

S1: KMS timeouts (data plane)
- Inject 2s, then 5s KMS client timeout on encrypt/decrypt path
- Expected: increased latency but bounded; breaker transitions to half-open/open at thresholds; no sustained elevated decrypt failure rate

S2: Throttling / 429s
- Inject throttling responses at 5% then 20% rate
- Expected: adaptive backoff reduces error spikes; breaker opens if sustained; retries do not amplify p95 latency beyond SLO for more than N minutes

S3: AccessDenied / IAM deny
- Inject AccessDenied for specific key alias / tenant
- Expected: fast-fail with clear error classification; no infinite retry; per-tenant impact visible; on-call knows when to page Security

S4: Key disabled
- Simulate disabled key error for currently pinned key version
- Expected: dual-read / bounded fallback behavior (if in rotation window); clear operator path (roll back pinned key version / switch to emergency key)

S5: Regional endpoint outage
- Simulate all KMS calls failing in region for 10 minutes
- Expected: breaker open; cache TTL mitigation option documented; graceful degradation per runbook; no cascading failure to unrelated tenants

Success criteria
- Alerts: correct severity, not noisy; triggers within 3–5 minutes for real brownout conditions
- Containment: per-tenant impact summaries available; no cross-tenant blast radius beyond shared dependencies
- Runbook usability: on-call can identify scenario, take safe mitigations (flags/TTL/breaker config) and determine when to escalate
- Evidence: audit events emitted for failures/denies and key usage; logs contain key IDs in sanitized form

Rollback / stop conditions
- Sustained decrypt failure rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes in canary OR any data corruption signals
- Breaker thrash (open/close oscillation) causing request amplification
- Any indication canary is affecting shared staging tenants outside test scope

Execution notes / timeline
2025-03-12
- 09:00 PT pre-brief complete; feature flags confirmed: kms_breaker_enabled=true, kms_failure_injection_enabled=true (staging + canary)
- 09:20 PT S0 baseline: dashboards confirmed; KMS p95 stable; cache hit ~92% decrypt, ~0% encrypt (expected)
- 09:35 PT S1 timeouts (2s then 5s): breaker opened at ~3m into 5s window; latency alert fired; no page (correct)
- 10:05 PT S2 throttling 5% then 20%:
  - At 20% saw retry amplification in one worker pool; p95 exceeded target for ~6m in staging; canary remained within error budget
  - Action: tightened max retries from 5 -> 3 for canary via config override; improved stability
- 10:40 PT S3 AccessDenied (tenant-scoped):
  - Correct classification in logs/metrics; per-tenant summary endpoint showed impacted tenant; Security escalation guidance confirmed
- 11:15 PT S4 disabled key simulation:
  - Observed elevated decrypt failures in canary-private-usw2-01 (peaked ~1.3% for ~4m) due to misconfigured dual-read ordering for one artifact type (metadata blob decrypt attempted only with new key)
  - Stop condition hit; rolled back rotation flag for canary; error rate recovered within 2m
  - Marcus/Kevin confirmed no data loss; failure was “can’t decrypt” not “bad decrypt”
- 12:10 PT S5 regional outage simulation: validated breaker behavior; runbook mitigation (temporary cache TTL extension) worked; decision: do not apply TTL extension by default (risk: stale crypto material) but keep as emergency lever

Key learnings
- Retry amplification risk under sustained throttling; need stricter defaults and clearer guidance on safe tuning knobs (max retries, max in-flight)
- Dual-read coverage gaps by artifact type need explicit test cases + a “rotation completeness” checklist (Private especially)
- Alerts were slightly delayed for tenant-scoped failure (AccessDenied) because global error rate stayed low; need per-tenant error spike alerting for canary tiers
- Runbook is usable but missing a “quick triage decision tree” (Timeout vs Throttle vs Deny vs DisabledKey) and explicit evidence to capture (breaker state, key id/alias, error codes)

Follow-ups (create/track separate issues)

- [x] ENG-4269: Tighten retry defaults under throttling; document safe override ranges; add load test

Final outcome
Game day completed. Staging scenarios executed end-to-end. Canary run surfaced a real rotation gap (artifact-type-specific dual-read), triggering an appropriate rollback and producing concrete fixes. No data loss observed; audit events and dashboards provided sufficient evidence for postmortem.
